reason: At 5% and 10% of all 512 queries, the saved R2 top score retrieves 1/39 and 3/39 repair opportunities, below random expectation within the 422 score-eligible queries, and yields 4 and 8 quality breaks. This is insufficient evidence to justify expanding expensive Target labels solely for this gate.
scope: Only the saved R2 best-action absolute-success score is tested. No full candidate-bag scores or encoder checkpoint were saved; no claim about all deployment-visible features or paired models.
next: Freeze one cheap candidate-set, relative-to-V8 signal audit on existing 512 train-side labels before deciding whether to spend Target calls on the remaining training queries. Keep quality repair and token-only saving separate.
